messages.subject: inla.group.cv - post-estimation
parts:
Hi prof Rue,

This is in connection with ' inla.group.cv'. This has greatly simplified resolving the 'failures' in computing cpo for some data point reducing computing time more efficiently.  I have some difficulties in obtaining the model outcomes for reporting. Appreciate your in great help in the following aspects. 

At present after running  'inla.group.cv', we are unable to see the model outcomes such as DIC, WAIC, estimates of fixed effects and hyperparameters, and quantiles. I would be grateful if you could kindly provide the code for getting the (i) DIC, (ii) WAIC, (iii) estimates for the fixed effects and hyperparameters and (iv) the 95% credible intervals for the linear predictor from the model output. It would be of great help while reporting model outcomes.

Thanks and regards,
ssubra

the cv estimates using inla(..., control.compute=list(cpo=T)) will be a
little different from the ones you get from inla.group.cv(), as the
internal approximations are different.

Dear Prof Rue,

Thanks for your quick response.  

I have taken your example and code for my question (given below). I have compared the output from the initial model 'r' and the final model 's' (after running 'inla.group.cv'). Please see the attached 'csv' file. I do not know how to get the quantiles for the mean based on model 's'. Also means from models' 's' and 'r' are different. Kindly guide me in  this respect.

Best regards
ssubra

###########################################################################################
### Havard Rue: Fitting models with LEAVE GROUP ONE OUT CROSS VALIDATION (LGOOCV) vs LOOCV)
### for assessing model performance - AN EXAMPLE comparing LOOCV vs LGOOCV)
###########################################################################################
rm(list = ls())
library(INLA)
data(Germany)
g = system.file("demodata/germany.graph", package="INLA")
source(system.file("demodata/Bym-map.R", package="INLA"))
Germany$id <- 1:nrow(Germany)
formula3 = Y ~ f(region, model="besag", graph=g) + f(id) + f(x,
                                                             model="rw2")

## just to get 'cpo' for comparison
r = inla(formula3, family="poisson", data=Germany, E=E,
         control.compute = list(cpo = TRUE,dic=TRUE,waic=TRUE))
cpo <- r$cpo$cpo

s = inla(formula3, family="poisson", data=Germany, E=E) #control.compute = list(cpo = TRUE,dic=TRUE,waic=TRUE))
s <- inla.group.cv(r)

plot(cpo,  s$cv, log = "xy", pty = 19)
abline(a = 0, b = 1, lwd = 3)

Germany$mean_s <-s[["mean"]]
Germany$sd_s <-s[["sd"]]
Germany$CV_s<-s[["cv"]]
#### How to get quantiles for the mean in model 's'?

Germany$mean_r <-r[["summary.fitted.values"]][, "mean"]
Germany$sd_r <-r[["summary.fitted.values"]][, "sd"]
Germany$LL_r <-r[["summary.fitted.values"]][, "0.025quant"]
Germany$ML_r <-r[["summary.fitted.values"]][, "0.5quant"]
Germany$UL_r <-r[["summary.fitted.values"]][, "0.975quant"]

write.csv(Germany,file="G:\\VL model_2\\vicente_52_models\\Modified_data_covariate_avg\\Output_E\\models with covariates\\Germany_11_apr_2023_E.csv")
###########################################################################################

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: inla.group.cv - post-estimation
parts:
I think its just a confusion, as inla.group.cv() just return the cv-
results and you overwrote the 's'. if you store them in 's$cv' you're
fine.

Please find attached the modified code. Also note that the 'E=E'
argument is not part of the fitted values. if you want that, then its
easier to instead of E=E, add

... + offset(log(E))

to the formula

hope this helps
Havard
